+++ b/app/controllers/invoices_controller.rb
@@ -8,6 +8,10 @@ class InvoicesController < ApplicationController

expectations: Response flags the missing organization scope in #show as critical or high severity, not minor
Response describes the concrete failure scenario: a user from one organization can fetch another organization's invoice by id
Response's suggested fix scopes through current_user.organization.invoices.find(params[:id]), consistent with the existing #index method
Response references the file and line (app/controllers/invoices_controller.rb around the new #show method)

evals.prompt:
Here's the issue this PR closes:

```
Title: Allow org admins to deactivate a member
Acceptance Criteria:
1. An org admin can deactivate another member of their own org.
2. A non-admin cannot deactivate anyone (403).
3. A deactivated member cannot log in.
```

And here's the diff, plus the only test file that touches this:

```diff
diff --git a/src/routes/members.ts b/src/routes/members.ts
index aaa1111..bbb2222 100644
--- a/src/routes/members.ts
+++ b/src/routes/members.ts
@@ -10,6 +10,14 @@ router.get('/members', requireAuth, listMembers)
+router.post('/members/:id/deactivate', requireAuth, requireOrgAdmin, async (req, res) => {
+  const member = await db.member.update({
+    where: { id: req.params.id },
+    data: { active: false },
+  })
+  res.json(member)
+})
diff --git a/src/routes/members.test.ts b/src/routes/members.test.ts
index ccc3333..ddd4444 100644
--- a/src/routes/members.test.ts
+++ b/src/routes/members.test.ts
@@ -20,3 +20,10 @@ describe('POST /members/:id/deactivate', () => {
+  it('deactivates a member as an admin', async () => {
+    const res = await request(app).post(`/members/${member.id}/deactivate`).set(adminAuth)
+    expect(res.status).toBe(200)
+  })
+  it('rejects a non-admin', async () => {
+    const res = await request(app).post(`/members/${member.id}/deactivate`).set(memberAuth)
+    expect(res.status).toBe(403)
+  })
})
```

Does this fully satisfy the acceptance criteria?
evals.expected_output: Acceptance criterion 3 ('a deactivated member cannot log in') has no test and should be flagged as high severity — the two existing tests only cover criteria 1 and 2. The response should also note that the deactivate route has no organization-scoping check on the member being deactivated (an org admin could deactivate a member of a different org), which is a critical/high finding in its own right, separate from the missing test.
expectations: Response identifies that acceptance criterion 3 ('deactivated member cannot log in') has no corresponding test
Response marks the missing test for criterion 3 as high severity
Response separately flags that the deactivate endpoint doesn't verify the target member belongs to the admin's own organization
Response does not credit the two existing tests as covering criterion 3
Response's test-coverage finding explains that a test must assert the behavior, not just call the endpoint
